19 March 2026

ECB staff macroeconomic projections for the euro area, March 2026

1 Overview

Inflation is projected to remain elevated in the short term, mainly reflecting higher energy prices. If the price of oil declines in line with prices in the futures market, inflation should return to the 2% target over the projection horizon. The outlook, however, is highly uncertain.

Economic growth is expected to recover gradually. Activity is projected to pick up over the projection horizon, supported by rising real incomes and the improving global environment.

2 Macroeconomic projections for the euro area economy

2.1 Real economy

Real GDP growth is projected to increase from 1.2% in 2026 to 1.4% in 2027 and 1.6% in 2028.

2.2 Prices and costs

Headline inflation is projected to average 2.0% in 2026, 1.9% in 2027 and 2.1% in 2028. HICP inflation excluding energy and food is projected to decline gradually from 2.6% in 2025 to 2.0% in 2028.
